messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — Multiple GPU host reboots in us-central1 (project: rw-inference-prod). Trigger: node reboots + PCIe AER in host logs. Paging infra-oncall and sre_taylor. Link: https://incidents.redwood/1767004321

infra-oncall: ack, working it. collecting initial node list.

sre_taylor: I'm on call. timeline? which zones/hosts?

infra-oncall: early hits at ~2025-11-03T02:12Z. Affected k8s nodes: gpu-pool-uc1-12, gpu-pool-uc1-17, gpu-pool-uc1-21. All in us-central1-a. Pods evicted: model-serving-prod v2 (several restarts), some batch jobs timed out.

eng-runtime-ops: seeing spike in 5xx from model endpoints, many streaming connections drop. Telemetry: token latency spikes to ~3x baseline. Customer-facing alerts: two high-tier customers reported degraded throughput.

ml_infra_ana: pasted quick log snippet from GPU node (dmesg):
```
[  932.123456] pcieport 0000:87:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received: ID 0000
[  932.123460] pcieport 0000:87:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Uncorrected (Non-Fatal), type=Transaction Layer, id=0000
[  932.123465] pcieport 0000:87:00.0: firmware: resetting link
[  932.123800] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x01:0x92:114)
[  932.124000] GPU-1234: GPU reset required, performing reset
[  932.300000] kernel: machine rebooted
```

cloud-gcp-eng: GCP incident console shows host-agent reboot and KVM reload events around the same timestamps for three hosts. There's an active GCP maintenance window? Not that I can see. Filing ticket with GCP infra now (case RW-1767004321).

support-aaron: customer-ops reported request IDs: rq-8f3a, rq-8f4b that saw 503s and aborted streams. I've DM'd affected customers with incident stub.

sre_taylor: ok hypothesis 1: noisy neighbor causing PCIe link flaps on host NIC/GPU bridge leading to hypervisor reset. Hypothesis 2: host firmware bug triggered by kernel PCIe AER handling during certain GPU workloads. Hypothesis 3: memory ECC corrected errors escalating to uncorrectable? any ECC traces?

ml_infra_ana: ECC counters (from nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory_ecc.errors): returned count increments on affected hosts: corrected_errors=235 -> 1187 in last 30m. No immediate uncorrectable reported but nvhost logs show repeated recoveries.

eng-runtime-ops: capturing pod-level stacks for affected model-serving pods and streaming sessions. Pasting kube events snippet:
```
LastSeen   TYPE    REASON             OBJECT
02:12Z     Warning EvictionReason     pod/model-serving-prod-abc - NodeRestart
02:12Z     Normal  Killing            pod/model-serving-prod-abc - Container exited
```

infra-oncall: mitigation step 1: cordon+drain remaining nodes in gpu-pool-uc1 (uc1-23..uc1-30) to prevent further restarts. Starting migration for critical customer routes to dedicated reserved pool in us-east1 as temporary fallback.

product-ops: do we have safe fallback for streaming contracts? need to notify customers if throughput will be reduced by ~50% for the next 2 hours.\
eng-runtime-ops: applied routing policy change: route model-serving-prod v2 -> fallback-model-small in us-east1 for affected customers. Triggered automatic cache warmup. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: deploy-bot initiated config change: route-update-1767004321 by eng-runtime-ops. CI/CD link: https://ci.internal/changes/1767004321

deploy-bot: canary rollout passed (5/5 requests) in us-east1 for fallback-model-small.

sre_taylor: timeline so far (building):
- 02:12Z first node reboot observed (gpu-pool-uc1-12) -> k8s pod evictions and 5xx spikes
- 02:14Z gpu-pool-uc1-17 rebooted
- 02:19Z gpu-pool-uc1-21 rebooted
- 02:25Z spike in corrected ECC counters across pool
- 02:30Z eng-runtime routing change in place, mitigation started
- 03:05Z partial recovery, but one host flapping still at 03:11Z

ml_infra_ana: adding logs bundle to GCS: gcs://redwood-incidents/1767004321/logs.tar.gz (dmesg, nv-host, journalctl, node-exporter).

cloud-gcp-eng: GCP support responded: they see a hardware error pattern on host chassis linked to PCIe fabric resets. They requested serial console logs and host UUIDs. Asked us to cordon/evacuate affected hosts.

infra-oncall: doing full evacuation of gpu-pool-uc1-12/17/21. Starting node replacement request with cloud-gcp-eng.

sre_taylor: hypothesis ranking for RCA thread: 1) host-level PCIe fabric instability triggered by underlying chassis hardware (favored: GCP corroborates), 2) GPU driver regression on our image (less likely: other tenants affected too), 3) workload pattern causing increased ECC corrected errors leading to reset (possible but secondary).

eng-runtime-ops: note: we saw a particular batch workflow using sustained high-bandwidth copies (model checkpoint restore) on 02:10Z from batch-job-44. That coincides with first reboot. Adding batch-job-44 logs to the bundle.

support-aaron: updated affected customer list in incident doc. Notified account teams for two enterprise customers on reserved capacity — they're being moved to dedicated reserved pool.

product-ops: prep post-incident comms (short and long). Please keep customer-impact counts (RPS affected, avg latency delta) in the incident doc.

sre_taylor: handoff: I'm wrapping initial triage; handing to eng-runtime-ops for deeper RCA and to coordinate long-term remediation. infra-oncall please post the final node host IDs and GCP ticket number here before I drop off.

infra-oncall: handing to eng-runtime-ops. GCP ticket: 1234567890. Affected host UUIDs: host-uuid-0a1b2c, host-uuid-0a1b2d, host-uuid-0a1b2f.

eng-runtime-ops: acknowledged. We'll coordinate kernel/driver dump analysis and post action items. Immediate follow-ups:
- upload serial console logs to GCS (in progress)
- request host replacement / maintainers to apply PCIe firmware patch if provided by cloud
- consider scheduling a rolling reboot across gpu-pool-uc1 to clear flapping hosts (only after replacement confirmed)

ml_infra_ana: adding small reproduction notes: batch-job-44 uses cudaMemcpyAsync patterns with sustained PCIe bandwidth ~90% for >10 minutes. Suggest test in staging on similar image to see if we can induce ECC increment.

sre_taylor: leaving final note: incident declared resolved at 03:07Z for customer-facing availability (traffic routed away). Still keeping RCA open until cloud confirms hardware cause and we decide on firmware or host replacement rollout. Posting incident slack summary to #postmortems when RCA draft is ready. :memo:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> ongoing RCA. Participants: sre_taylor, eng-runtime-ops, infra-oncall, cloud-gcp-eng.

eng-runtime-ops: next steps assigned in issue tracker: ISSUE-1767004321 (RCA writeup), ISSUE-1767004322 (firmware/host replacement plan), ISSUE-1767004323 (improve detection for PCIe AER thresholding).

support-aaron: closing customer pings for now; will escalate if any regressions.

product-ops: thanks team. keep updates in this thread for the RCA doc.

sre_taylor: signing off from on-call, handing pager to infra-oncall. :wave:

infra-oncall: taking pager. will follow up with cloud ticket updates and final host replacement ETA.

eng-runtime-ops: uploading collected artifacts now, ping when uploaded.

incident-bot: logs uploaded: https://gcs.console/1767004321/logs.tar.gz (permissions: restricted).

sre_taylor: final checklist for RCA: timeline, root cause hypothesis (with evidence), customer impact summary, mitigation actions taken, and follow-ups. please tag me on the draft.

eng-runtime-ops: ACK. I'll create draft and link back here.

(reacts: many messages received :thumbsup: and :eyes:)
